text:
zoe: quick thread: we need to pick the observability MVP slice that most reduces customer pain for launch. i see three distinct asks: 1) near-real-time cost-anomaly detection (finance + platform), 2) regression detection for error rates tied to model rollouts (ml/product), 3) lightweight trace links for fast triage. which one is highest impact?

dan: for me, regression detection tied to rollouts is #1. customers keep shipping model versions and then seeing silent quality regressions. if we can auto-detect a stat significant uptick in error-rate or degradation in top-k accuracy vs baseline within 30m that's huge. dashboards alone don't catch that quickly.

kai: auto-detecting regressions implies we need historical baselines, smoothing windows, and a signal store. That's more infra than a cost dashboard. cost-anomaly (spikes) is cheaper: simple aggregations + z-score alerts.

anya: suggestion: two-phase MVP. Phase A = cost anomaly + alerting + exportable incident CSV. Phase B = rollout-aware regression detection that hooks into rollout metadata (model.version, canary percent) + optional short traces on alerted windows. Phase A can be done in 2 sprints, Phase B in 3-4.

zoe: good. minimum acceptance for Phase A (cost-anomaly):
- real-time windowed aggregation (1m granularity) for cost and tokens
- anomaly detector: rolling z-score threshold default=3, adjustable per-tenant
- alert sink: webhook + slack + incidents console with CSV export
- dashboard widgets (top 10 anomalies last 24h) and per-tenant drilldown
- perf: aggregation adds <2% p95 tail

dan: and Phase B (regression-detection) acceptance: 
- baseline model metrics (error-rate, latency, top-k correctness) computed per model.version and route
- statistical test (e.g., fisher or chi-sq) to detect uplift with configurable alpha (default 0.01)
- auto-link to last 5 sampled traces for the window when regression detected
- rollout metadata ingestion so we can correlate canary % with metric delta
- false positive rate <= 10% on synthetic eval harness

kai: infra note: regression detection needs a metric store with per-minute counters and a lightweight evaluation runner. sampling for traces should be "on_alert" rather than global to keep storage low. propose sampling config:
```
tracing.global_sampling = 0.001 # 0.1% baseline
tracing.on_alert_sampling = 1.0
anomaly.window = 1m
anomaly.method = "rolling_z"
regression.test = "chi2"
```

anya: operational rollout: Phase A canary at 10% of customers for 1 week; Phase B internal canary 5% traffic 2 weeks, because regression detector can trigger lots of alerts. Need playbook for triage (who owns the alert: infra vs ml vs customer).

monitor-bot: prototype run results: staging 20k rps with anomaly window 1m -> aggregation CPU +0.6%, p95 +0.9%. Trace storage when on_alert sampling used ~8GB/day for canary cohort.

zoe: launch risk checklist: data correctness (aggregation gaps <0.1%), latency (p95 delta <2%), ops burden (avg alerts/day per 10k customers <5), cost (infra delta <=8% for beta), and ownership playbooks exist.

dan: UX asks: two templates out of gate: Incident-ops (for SRE triage) and ML-regressions (shows model.version, metric deltas, linked examples). Make the regression alert include a quick "compare" view: baseline vs current histogram.

kai: engineering asks: 2 backend for anomaly engine + regression runner, 1 infra for benching, 1 frontend for widgets and compare-view. estimate Phase A = 2 sprints, Phase B = 4 sprints. need a small synthetic harness to validate false-positive rates.

product-bot: ticket created https://tracker/redwood/PRD-900 "obs-mvp: phaseA cost-anomaly + phaseB rollout-regression-detector" assignees: zoe, kai, anya.

zoe: ok locking plan: ship Phase A (cost-anomaly) in next beta, include Phase B in roadmap with internal canary. if no objections i'll add the launch criteria and the alert playbook to the roadmap doc tonight. speak now before i lock. :lock:
